title: Inertial confinement driver efficiency and repetition rate
bottleneck: Laser inertial fusion must deliver megajoules to targets with high wall-plug efficiency and fire several times per second. The National Ignition Facility's lasers are roughly 1 percent efficient and fire a few times per day. Diode-pumped solid-state and excimer laser concepts promise better efficiency, but no driver has demonstrated the combination of energy, efficiency, repetition rate, and durability a power plant needs. Driver cost and lifetime dominate inertial fusion economics.
why_it_blocks: An inertial fusion plant lives or dies on its driver. At 1 percent efficiency the plant consumes more power than it makes, and at one shot per day it produces no meaningful energy regardless of target gain.
current_state: NIF achieved ignition in 2022, and rep-rated laser architectures are in development at national labs and startups, but a power-plant-class driver remains a paper concept.
